title: Choose jiffkit's new look
question: New hand: the roll landed on The Tool Wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each card's picture is the homepage layout.

options.label: The Tool Wall
options.lineage: workshop pegboards with painted tool outlines
options.thesis: Every tool hangs in its own painted outline on one wall, so you always know where it lives and that it never leaves the workshop.
materials: painted outline shadows (large Lucide line icons)
options.viewport: Homepage: a full-width pegboard with a dot grid; each tool hangs in its outline inside a taped zone (Image, PDF, AI, Video, Developer); a stencilled line reads NOTHING LEAVES THE WORKSHOP. Tool page: that tool lifted off the wall onto a bench mat that is the drop zone.
options.risk: Can tip into cute skeuomorphism, and a dot grid behind 42 tools can feel busy without strict zones.

raised.raise: Colour at page scale: each zone owns a full flat field of its tape colour, not a sprinkle of accents.
Edge codes: every tool carries a stamped code (IMG-01, PDF-03) used in its URL hint and on its page.
Banded steps: each tool page stacks its steps as horizontal courses, one per action.
Visible before it happens: the bench shows what will come out (format, size) before you run it.

options.label: The Line Map
options.lineage: metro maps and transit wayfinding signage
options.thesis: Every tool is a station on a coloured line (Image, PDF, AI, Video, Developer), so finding one is reading a map you already know how to read.
options.viewport: Homepage: a full-width route map, five coloured lines with every tool as a labelled station and interchanges where tools connect (HEIC → JPG to PDF). Tool page: a station sign header with its line colour and 'next stations' as related tools.
options.risk: Familiar: the subway-map metaphor is a well-worn infographic, and 42 stations must stay legible on a phone.

regions.label: Developer line: 29 stations in two loops

options.label: The Passport
options.lineage: well-travelled passports: visa pages, entry stamps, security paper
options.thesis: Every file you process gets an official stamp: PROCESSED ON THIS DEVICE, dated, never sent.
options.viewport: Homepage: a passport data page as the hero (jiffkit's 'holder' details: 42 tools, 0 uploads, in OCR-B), with visa pages below as tool categories.
options.case: Holds audience identification (a passport means trust and officialdom, which answers 'not trustworthy enough') but loses product clarity: stamps and visas don't say which tool does what.
options.risk: Ornamental if the stamps are decoration; security-paper patterns are heavy to render well.

options.label: Cut-paper Title Cards
options.thesis: One idea per full-bleed colour card, told in cut-paper shapes.
options.viewport: Timed full-bleed cards, one per tool group.
options.case: Strong brand, but cards hide 42 tools behind a sequence; neither audience can scan it.
options.kept: Colour at page scale: each zone owns a full flat field.

options.label: Hand-processed Film
options.thesis: Every conversion as a strip of frames.
options.viewport: A film strip of tool frames.
options.case: Only the video tools relate; it says nothing about privacy.
options.kept: Edge codes: every tool carries a stamped code.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: The site as courses of clay rising.
options.case: Neither audience sees tools or privacy in clay.
options.kept: Banded steps: tool pages stack their steps as courses.

options.label: Live-code Floor
options.thesis: The page as a projected code buffer.
options.viewport: A code buffer as the homepage.
options.case: Developers might connect; everyday visitors would leave. It is also the dark neon rut.
options.kept: Visible before it happens: the bench shows the output before you run it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What iLovePDF and Smallpdf ship: a clean grid of coloured tool cards, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A headline, category chips and a grid of icon cards: the arrangement visitors already expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design, which is the problem you named.
